1199: Even if the one I long for shows me no kindness, anything I hear about him is still sweet to my ears.
1200: Long live you, my heart! Telling your great pain to someone who does not care about you is like trying to fill up the sea.
1221: Long live you, evening! But you are not really evening at all. You are a deadly time that eats up the lives of wives whose husbands are far away.
1222: Long live you, confused evening! Your eyes look dim and sad like mine. Is your partner as hard-hearted as my husband?
1223: The pale evening comes as drops of dew begin to form. With it, my distress begins to grow, and my sorrow keeps getting bigger.
1241: My heart, won't you think hard and tell me some medicine, any kind at all, that can cure this sickness of sorrow?
1246: My heart, when you see the one you love, who ends our sulking by holding us close, you cannot even stay upset. So the anger you show him now is fake.
1247: My good heart, either let go of your love or let go of your modesty. I cannot carry both of them at once.
1251: My self-control was like a door locked tight with the bolt of modesty. But the axe of love smashes that door down.
1257: When the one I love, out of love, does the things I long for, I no longer know anything called modesty.
1272: My innocent love, whose beauty fills my eyes and whose shoulders are smooth like bamboo, is full of a deep womanly modesty.
1293: My heart, is it because "people who are ruined have no friends" that you leave me and follow him as you please?
1297: My silly heart has no dignity and cannot forget him. Stuck with such a heart, I have even forgotten my modesty.
1305: Even for good men with fine qualities, the real beauty is the sulking that rises in the hearts of their wives with flower-like eyes.
1306: Love without its deep sulks and light sulks is like fruit that is either too ripe or still hard and green.
